_doc: picture-qa per-shot config template. Copy to the project (docs/picture-qa.shots.json), replace the example scenes/shots with the project's shot table. Frame names: <scene>_t<seconds>.png (picture-qa --url --scene ID writes this), t<seconds>.png, or frame-<n>.png with fps. Merge: built-in < defaults < scene < shot < command line. luma = Rec.709 luma of encoded 0..1 values: lo/hi mean band, p99min brightest 1% floor, p01max darkest 1% ceiling, drmin p99-p01 floor. warmMax = warm-pixel fraction budget. sky = 'auto' | 'none' | top fraction | {rects}. Every exemption (allowStripes, skip, sky other than auto, warmMax or any luma bound looser than these defaults) must name its basis in 'exempt' (designed-texture | real-light | non-sky-region) and say in '_why' what in the picture justifies it; the thresholds below are the template defaults and anything looser is listed in report.json. Never relax a threshold or shrink the sky to make a frame pass: change the picture. Validate with: picture-qa.mjs --check-config FILE [--baseline previous.json] (alerts on any shrink or relaxation vs the previous config).

exterior._why: night exterior: one point of warmth (a lamp), everything else cold

shots.name: A2 long lens ground
shots._roi: ground area of the current fix; with --compare it must change

shots.name: A3 wall close
shots._why: close wall shot: the courses are the designed regular texture and the frame contains no sky

allowStripes.why: designed layered wall courses (regular horizontal texture)

shots._sky: no horizon in frame: wall/ground edge must not be taken as horizon

dawn._why: warm dawn light is the design: the low sun is a real light source in frame

shots.name: B1 upward sky
shots._why: upward framing: no horizon line, the lower 15% is the ridge, declare the sky
